subject: Multiple trees and multiple set of dispersal multipliers and time periods

messages.author: 7be2e4526c1a9416
messages.subject: Multiple trees and multiple set of dispersal multipliers and time periods
parts:
Dear Dr. Nicholas Matzke,

We are running our BioGeoBEARS analyses taking into account different dispersal multipliers in different time periods.

We are having a problem running the analyses having into account multiple trees. The problem is that some of the trees are younger than the second age we indicate in the time period file. That makes the analysis to crash. We have tried to add a root edge to all phylogenies but does not solve the problem.

I think there are several alternatives:
- Several time periods files and dispersal multipliers files that match with each of trees in the tree set.
- To ignore the fact that thera are time periods that are not present in some of the trees.
- To allow to have root edge in the trees.

Thank you very much for any thought.

Cheers,

Marcial. 

--

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Multiple trees and multiple set of dispersal multipliers and time periods
parts:
Hi -- yeah, BioGeoBEARS runs some checks on the root node to make sure it is within the oldest time bin.  There might be a way to recode that to look at the root branch, but I think it would be complex as most trees won't have root branches.

The simpler strategy would be to set up your time-bins such that the oldest time-bin covers the root node no matter which tree is used. 

A question to ask yourself is: does the geography really change significantly near the bottom of the tree, in a way that is likely to really matter for your biogeographical analysis?  After all, a time-bin covering the root probably only contains a tiny part of the tree anyway.  Perhaps you could just merge the bottom two time-bins or something like that. (Note: a simple option is to always set the bottom time of the oldest time bin to something very large, way larger than the root of any of your trees -- 500 my or something.)

If for some reason it really is important to keep the bottom time bin, then the easiest solution would be to just use an if/then statement in your R script looping through the trees. Something like:

# Make a tree table containing the node ages
tree_table = prt(tr)

# The root age is the maximum node age:
root_age = max(tree_table$time_bp)

# Let's say the last time bin starts at 10 mya
if (root_age > 10)
{
times_fn = "time_file_with_bottom_time_bin.txt"
} else {
times_fn = "time_file_without_bottom_time_bin.txt"
}

...etc...

Cheers!
Nick
